findings.title: Kill trip while a strategy CLOSE order is in flight: loop crash + double-sell risk
findings.claim: When RiskKillSwitch trips with a non-terminal close OrderTask: _kill_sequence cancels the task but never clears self._task, and _book_flatten_closes closes the very position the close targets; the close task's next terminal poll calls PaperBook.close_position on an already-closed position -> ExecError propagates to on_tick step 6 and crashes the loop. Deeper: the kill submits flatten-<symbol> while the strategy close (o-/synthetic-o-) sell is also live -> a genuine concurrent broker double-sell / 'may flatten, never flip' violation.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py _kill_sequence (~1003-1047), _book_flatten_closes (~1049-1087), _terminal (~1538-1543); paper_book.py:350-353 (the raise). Repro: synthetic ExecPipeline, open 10 AAPL, install a close _OrderTask in 'watch' for that position_id, trigger_kill('drill') -> position closed but close task survives -> feed it a terminal filled BrokerOrder -> ExecError: position pos-... is closed (terminal).
findings.fix: Kill sequence retires a non-terminal CLOSE task (the cancel makes the kill the single flatten of record; never two concurrent sells on one position; an OPEN task is kept for the M5C-S11 late-fill tripwire). _terminal's close path guards with a position-still-open check -> a superseded close logs order_state_alert{note:'close_superseded_position_closed'} instead of crashing. Pinned in test_kill_flatten_driver.py: kill with a CLOSE in flight -> position ends flat, loop survives, no double-sell.

findings.title: Over-qty ExitInstruction crashed the tick loop permanently
findings.claim: _start_close calls mint_reduce_only_token(position, intent) UNGUARDED; an ExitInstruction with qty > held raises PreflightRejected ('reduce-only qty must be >0 and <= held size') that escapes _start_close -> _exits -> on_tick and crashes the loop; a re-emitting ExitProvider re-crashes every subsequent tick (loop permanently wedged).
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:~1757 (the unguarded mint). Repro: paper ExecPipeline, RealStrategyStub opens 10, ReEmittingExitProvider qty=20 -> 'CRASH in on_tick: PreflightRejected'; every later tick re-crashes. The mint correctly REFUSES the oversized sell (fail-closed direction intact), but the crash stalls all subsequent reductions.
findings.fix: Wrapped the mint in try/except PreflightRejected; on raise journal order_state_alert{raw_status:'reduce_only_mint_rejected', note:'reduce_qty_exceeds_held'} and return (self._task still None). Loop survives, no submit, position intact. Chose order_state_alert (free-form note, §P.2) over a fabricated reject reason — EXTRA_REJECT_REASONS has no member apt for qty>held and exec_reasons stays unedited.

findings.title: Close path never fed a modeled fill -> §J/EX-9 sell fees + close fill_divergence were dead in integrated runs
findings.claim: _terminal and _book_flatten_closes called close_position(modeled=None); _start_close never computed a sell-side model_fill. So FeeModel sell path + close_position EX-9 fee math + close fill_divergence flag were reachable only by unit tests; every integrated/E2E close had zero sell fees and a hardcoded unassessed flag.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:1539-1543, 1084-1087 (modeled=None), 1551 (model_fill/assess on the open only). paper_book.close_position EX-9 fee path is correct + unit-tested in isolation (test_paper_book.py:479-481, 584-587) but never exercised end-to-end.
findings.fix: Close path computes a sell-side ModeledFill from the SAME quote_b/cap the close priced (no hindsight), binds the id, journals modeled_execution_fill, carries it on the close _OrderTask.modeled, passes it to close_position -> realized_modeled_pnl reflects the EX-9 sell fee (notional = modeled exit proceeds) and fill_divergence gets a real side-aware flag (EX-3). Kill-flatten keeps modeled=None (forced liquidation per §M.6/FD-M5-1, not a realism-scored decision). Synthetic goldens regenerated (fills.jsonl 5610->6753 B, positions.jsonl 7279->7285 B; orders unchanged; observe untouched; byte-stable double-run).

findings.title: FlattenUnpriced leaked the minted reduce-only token (registry hygiene)
findings.claim: PriceCappedFlattenBroker.submit_order raises FlattenUnpriced (unmapped symbol / no quote / unpriceable cap) WITHOUT voiding the already-minted reduce-only authorization; the M0 kill loop catches the exception and discards the token object, leaving the _authorizations entry resident for the process lifetime -> a slow leak across retry_residual passes. Harmless (reduce-only kind, unreachable after GC) but a leak.
findings.evidence: flatten_proxy.py:57-66 (raises before inner.submit_order consumes the token); kill_switch.py:41 already issued the authorization. The proxy may NOT import agent.execution_preflight (§3 import row).
findings.fix: Dependency injection: PriceCappedFlattenBroker ctor takes an optional void_token callable (default None -> no-op, existing construction/tests unaffected); before each raise FlattenUnpriced it calls self._void_token(token, 'no_price_for_cap') when provided. The orchestrator (which legitimately imports execution_preflight) passes execution_preflight.void_token when it builds the proxy in §M.6. 'no_price_for_cap' is a legal void reason (EXTRA_REJECT_REASONS). §3 import discipline respected (no execution_preflight import added to the proxy).

findings.title: Live-path credential key mismatch: read creds['secret'] but the frozen key is 'secret_key'
findings.claim: _build_real_client does TradingClient(secret_key=creds['secret'], ...) but the §O.2 / secrets_runtime frozen credential key set is exactly {key_id, secret_key, base_url}; load_alpaca_paper_credentials returns 'secret_key' and rejects extra keys, so creds['secret'] raises KeyError. Not exercised by the offline suite (the AST guard proves _build_real_client is the sole import-alpaca site, never reached offline), so 1513 tests stayed green; the credentialed path is M5-2a (deferred/unprovisioned).
findings.evidence: alpaca.py:196 (creds['secret']) vs secrets_runtime.py:53,134 (returns {key_id, secret_key, base_url}). key_id and base_url match; only secret_key->secret diverges.
findings.fix: alpaca.py:196 -> creds['secret_key']. Added a test_alpaca_adapter.py test that stubs the alpaca SDK (fake sys.modules, cleaned up so the purity test stays honest), feeds the frozen {key_id, secret_key, base_url} shape, and asserts the broker constructs without KeyError and secret_key flows through.

findings.title: fill_delta computed delta_cost under the ambient Decimal context (M4-DET-1 precedent not followed)
findings.claim: order_state.fill_delta computed the integrated-notional product under the ambient context while exec_ledger pins prec=28 for cum_notional_after. For all realistic equity qty x price they coincide and nothing in scripts/agent mutates the global context, so the telescoping invariant Sum delta_cost == final qty x avg holds and NO divergence is reproducible. Only a separate global-context corruption could surface it -> not a determinism defect, but it didn't follow the M4-DET-1 ambient-immunity precedent the contract cites.
findings.evidence: order_state.py fill_delta (delta_cost product under ambient context) vs exec_ledger.py:761-767 (pinned Context(prec=28)).
findings.fix: Wrapped the prev_cost/delta_cost products in localcontext(Context(prec=28, ROUND_HALF_EVEN)). Test: under a hostile ambient prec=3 context the product 70x100.18 stays exact at 4009.60 (would otherwise round to 7.01E+3).
